main_text.p: feuero tamque immani auxilio abstinen-dum esse censemus, & iis præsertim, unde bonæ prolis ipes est. Cæterum eorum, qui ipsam castrationem respuerint, generationis causa, articulos pharmacia, aut chirurgia confirmari par est. Quæ autem ad id conferunt pharmaca cogendi uim & comprimendi habere necesse est: quorum duplex genus statuimus. Nam alia exiccantia sunt, & astringentia: alia uero refrigerant, & indurant. Prioris generis uberrima extat sylua apud ueteres & recentiores medicos. Præ cæteris autem ad luxatos articulos Galenus octauo libro, de Simplicium medicamentorum facultatibus, phœnicis corticem cum foris admotum, cum intus assumptum mire commendat. Propterea articulorum imbecillitati plurimum auxiliari poteft. Nonnulli quoque celebres medici Germaniæ spongiosum quendam lapidem, qui in Hil debergæ fabulis frequens reperitur ad idé [?] foris admotum cum oui albumine, mastiche, & similibus glutinantibus non parui æstimant: eo quod fracta ossa mirifice cogat & agglutinet, quemadmodum etiā fatis experti fumus. page.notes: Catchword "menda," stands alone at the lower right and is kept out of the text. The last line ends without a printed hyphen; the catchword suggests "assumenda", so "assu" is kept as read. "idé" has an uncertain accent, marked [?]. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. Line 2 "ijs" is rendered "iis", and "Hil" in "qui in Hil" is kept as printed. Print shows light foxing and show-through from the reverse, which is not transcribed.
